title: Build Order
statement: A monorepo has 20,000 packages and 60,000 "depends on" links. The build system must find an order that builds every dependency before the packages that need it, or report that the links go in a circle.
examples: ui depends on core; core depends on utils → utils, core, ui

approaches.name: Kahn's algorithm: in-degrees and a queue of packages with none left
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: One pass; a short order at the end reveals a cycle.

approaches.name: Depth-first search, adding each package after all its dependencies (post-order)
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Also linear, but cycle detection needs extra colour states.

approaches.name: Repeatedly scan all packages for one whose dependencies are built
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but rescans everything after each build.

title: Nearest Exit
statement: A stadium floor plan is a 2,000 × 2,000 grid with walls and 300 exits. For the evacuation sign at every open cell, the system needs the fewest steps to any exit.
examples: Exits marked E; each open cell gets its distance

approaches.name: One BFS that starts with all exits in the queue at distance 0
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each cell is reached first from its nearest exit, in one pass.

approaches.name: One BFS from each exit, keeping the minimum per cell
approaches.label: valid

approaches.name: BFS from each cell until it finds an exit
approaches.label: valid

approaches.name: Straight-line distance to the nearest exit
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Ignores walls, so the numbers are wrong.

title: Fastest Delivery Route
statement: A courier map has 50,000 junctions and 200,000 one-way roads, each with a travel time in minutes (all positive). The app needs the fastest time from the depot to every junction.
examples: depot → A 5 min, depot → B 2 min, B → A 1 min → A is 3 min

approaches.name: Dijkstra's algorithm with a min-heap of tentative times
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each junction is final when it leaves the heap.

approaches.name: Relax every road V − 1 times (Bellman–Ford)
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, also handles negative times, but about 10 billion steps here.

approaches.name: BFS counting roads
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Fewest roads is not fastest when times differ.

approaches.name: DFS over every route, keeping the fastest
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Correct only by exhausting all routes, which is infeasible.
